post.description: Use to create a batch of courses, e.g. from an imported timetable.

delete.summary: Delete a course and all of its data (grades, files, schedule).
delete.description: Irreversible. Use only when the user clearly asks to delete the course.

get.summary: Get one course with its terms, credits, instructors and resolved color.
get.description: Use when you need the details of a course whose id you know.

patch.summary: Change a course's code, title, alias, credits, color, instructors or other fields.
patch.description:
Partial update: only the fields that are sent change. To move a course to other
terms or make it year-long, use academics.course.set_terms.

put.summary: Set the display order of the courses within a term.
put.description: Courses not listed keep their default order after the listed ones.

put.summary: Set which terms a course runs in (consecutive terms for a year-long course).
put.description:
Replaces the course's terms. They must belong to its Program and be next to each
other in time.

get.summary: List the user's Programs (degrees) with their term and course counts.
get.description:
Use to find the Program ids of the user, e.g. before listing terms or courses
when no Program is given. Most users have exactly one Program.

post.summary: Create a Program (a degree or study plan).
post.description:
Use only when the user explicitly wants a new, separate Program, e.g. a second
degree. Do not use to add a term or a course; use academics.term.create or
academics.course.create.

delete.summary: Delete a Program with all of its terms, courses and their data.
delete.description:
Irreversible. Use only when the user clearly asks to delete the whole Program.
To remove one term or course use academics.term.delete or academics.course.delete.

get.summary: Get one Program: name, school, time zone, credit defaults and subject colors.
get.description: Use when you need a Program's details such as its time zone or credit goal.

patch.summary: Change a Program's name, school, time zone or credit settings.
patch.description: Partial update: only the fields that are sent change.

put.summary: Set the color of a subject code (e.g. all 'APS' courses) in a Program.
put.description:
Use when the user wants every course of a subject in another color. To color a
single course differently, use academics.course.update with `color`.

get.summary: Week numbers of a term: each week's dates, number or break, and today's week.
get.description:
Use to translate between dates and week numbers ("week 6", "reading week"),
e.g. to resolve "the Friday of week 3". Week 1 is the week the term starts in.

post.summary: Create a term, optionally with its courses, in one step.
post.description:
Use when the user starts a new semester. Check academics.term.list first so the
term does not exist already. `courses` creates courses in the new term; `continue_course_ids`
extends year-long courses of the previous term into it.

get.summary: List the terms (semesters) of a Program in chronological order.
get.description:
Use to find a term id, or which term is current (`is_current`), before creating
courses or answering questions about a semester.

delete.summary: Delete a term and the courses that are only in it.
delete.description:
Irreversible. Year-long courses that also run in other terms are kept and only
lose this term. Show academics.term.delete_preview to the user first.

get.summary: Get one term with its dates and breaks.
get.description: Use when you need a term's dates, reading weeks or holidays.

patch.summary: Change a term's name, dates, breaks or week numbering.
patch.description:
Partial update. `breaks` replaces the whole list; keep the ids of breaks that
stay. Fails with academics.course_terms_not_adjacent when new dates would separate the terms of
a year-long course.

get.summary: What deleting a term would remove: its own courses vs. year-long courses kept.
get.description: Use before academics.term.delete to tell the user what will be deleted.

get.summary: Everything on the calendar in a date range: classes, events, deadlines, tasks.
get.description:
Use for "when is my class tomorrow?", "what's on next Wednesday?" or a week
overview. Interpret relative days in the Program's time zone and pass dates; `end` is exclusive
and at most 120 days after `start`. Cancelled classes are included with status 'cancelled'.
For today alone prefer calendar.today. Each class carries its term week in meta.week_number.

parameters.name: start

schema.description: First day, in the Program's time zone
schema.title: Start

parameters.description: First day, in the Program's time zone

parameters.name: end

schema.description: Day after the last day (exclusive); at most 120 days later
schema.title: End

parameters.description: Day after the last day (exclusive); at most 120 days later

schema.description: Sources to include, e.g. ['schedule.meetings', 'grading.assessments']; all by default
schema.title: Sources

parameters.description: Sources to include, e.g. ['schedule.meetings', 'grading.assessments']; all by default

get.summary: Today in a Program: classes and events, deadlines of the next 7 days, due tasks.
get.description:
Prefer this for questions about today ("what do I have today?", "what's due this
week?"). It also says which term week it is. For other days or longer ranges use
calendar.occurrences. Times are UTC; read them in the returned `timezone`.

post.summary: Cancel a pending or running background job.
post.description:
Use when the user wants to stop a background operation. A running job stops at
its next checkpoint, so it may still finish. Cancelling a finished job changes nothing.

schema.description: Job id, as returned when the job was started.

get.summary: Get the state and progress of a background job.
get.description:
Use to check on a long-running operation (file parsing, imports, syncs) that
another capability started and returned a job id for.

get.description:

get.summary: Get how much file storage the user has used and their quota.
get.description:
Use when the user asks how much space their files take or why an upload was
rejected for exceeding the quota.

get.summary: Class sections of a term that overlap each other.
get.description:
Use before or after adding meetings to warn about clashes. Only enabled sections
that share at least one date count.

post.summary: Add a one-off event: an exam, office hour, make-up class or appointment.
post.description:
Times without an offset are read in the Program's time zone. For something
that repeats weekly use schedule.meeting.create.

get.summary: List one-off events (exams, office hours, make-up classes) of a Program.

Optionally only one course's or one term's. For a date range use
calendar.occurrences.

delete.summary: Delete a custom type that no meeting or event uses.
delete.description: Fails with schedule.event_type_in_use while anything uses the type.

meeting.

post.summary: Create a read-only calendar subscription link (ICS) for Apple or Google Calendar.
post.description: Anyone with the link can read the calendar; it is returned only once.

get.summary: List the calendar subscription links of a Program.
get.description: The links themselves are only shown when created.

delete.summary: Turn off a calendar subscription link.
delete.description: Calendars subscribed to it stop updating.

post.summary: Add a weekly (or biweekly) class section to a course in one of its terms.
post.description:
Times are wall-clock times in the Program's time zone. Check
schedule.conflicts afterwards and mention any overlap. For a single extra session (exam, make-up
class) use schedule.event.create instead.

get.summary: List a course's weekly class sections, with their cancelled or moved dates.
get.description:
Use to see when a course meets each week, or to find the meeting id before
changing or cancelling one class. Optionally only one term of a year-long course.

post.summary: Add several class sections to a course at once (imports).
post.description:
Used by importers. An item with the same source_kind and source_ref as an
existing meeting of the course updates it instead of adding a duplicate.

delete.summary: Delete a class section with all its dates.
delete.description:
Removes the section entirely. To cancel one class use
schedule.exception.upsert with kind 'cancelled'; to hide a section the user does not attend use
schedule.meeting.set_enabled.

patch.summary: Change a class section for the whole term (time, room, weeks, ...).
patch.description:
Changes every week. To change or cancel a single date use
schedule.exception.upsert instead.

put.summary: Show or hide class sections of a course, e.g. keep only the user's tutorial.
put.description: Disabled sections stay in the course but are left out of the calendar.

get.summary: Get the user's personal preferences.
get.description:
Use when you need the user's language, clock format (12h/24h) or first day of
the week, for example to format a time or date in the way the user expects.
Do not use to read per-module settings such as the calendar default view;
use settings.values.get.

patch.summary: Change personal preferences (language, theme, accent, clock, week start).
patch.description: Partial update: only the fields that are sent change. Not for agents.

get.summary: List every settings namespace with its fields.
get.description:
Use before changing a module setting to find the namespace, the field names,
their allowed values and the levels (account, program, term, course) where they can be set.
Do not use to read current values; use settings.values.get.

post.summary: Read several UI state entries at once.
post.description:
Reads interface state (sort orders, collapsed panels) by key or key prefix.
Not available to agents.

put.description: Stores interface state under a key. Not available to agents.

Do not use for personal preferences such as language or theme; use settings.preferences.get.

Look up namespace and field names with settings.schemas.list first.
Do not use to change language, theme or other personal preferences.
